heroHeadline: Trump Suspends Diversity Visa Lottery Citing Brown University Gunman; NJ Officials Demand Delaney Hall Shutdown; DOJ Sues 4 States Over ICE Undercover License Plates
heroSubtitle: On May 29, 2026, New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, Senator Cory Booker, and other NJ officials formally demanded DHS shut down the Delaney Hall ICE detention facility in Newark after the state's health department was denied full access for an inspection — as the detainee labor strike entered its second week amid allegations of maggot-infested food, guard violence, and denied medical care. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin threatened to pull CBP officers from Newark Liberty International Airport to suppress the protests, a move the U.S. Travel Association warned would have 'devastating consequences'; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy also questioned the threat. Separately, the DOJ filed federal lawsuits against Maine, Massachusetts, Oregon, and Washington for refusing to issue undercover license plates to ICE and CBP agents, with the states arguing that confidential plates are reserved for criminal — not civil — law enforcement. The Senate's floor vote on the $71.7 billion ICE/CBP reconciliation package — the largest single-year immigration enforcement investment in U.S. history — remains imminent but still unscheduled, with Trump's June 1 signing deadline now effectively slipped to the week of June 1.
